475.title: Content
475.notes: Agenda includes trajectory, path contrast, continuity, joint/task schemes, cubic, quintic and linear. Heading typo “Join Space” is cosmetic.
475.excluded: Agenda only; no extra definition, equation or examinable example.

476.title: Trajectory Planning
476.notes: Read joint-time mapping theta_i(t), i=1..n,t in[0,tf]; initial/final configurations, feasibility, constraints, kinematic joint limits, bounded torque and derivative continuity.

477.title: Path VS Trajectory
477.notes: Path theta(s),s∈[0,1] lacks timing; trajectory theta(s(t)) includes time scaling. Diagram labels T=0,t1,t2,t3,t4,tf on solid route and dashed “Path” between same endpoints, but drawn routes differ geometrically: illustration must not override mathematical time-scaling preserving one specified path.

478.title: Continuity requirements
478.notes: C0/C1/C2 explicitly match position/velocity/acceleration left/right limits; nested smoothness presumed. Bottom asserts discontinuous acceleration gives infinite torque spikes, which conflicts with finite inertia dynamics and p479 finite discontinuity statement; preserve discrepancy.

479.title: Continuity Requirements (Contd..)
479.notes: Dynamics τ=M(Θ)Θddot+V(Θ,Θdot)+G(Θ); acceleration jump gives torque discontinuity; velocity jump requires ideal infinite/impulsive acceleration. Minimum C1, preferred C2. Must qualify finite model terms and distinguish jump from impulse.

480.title: Joint Space Schemes Vs Cartesian Space Schemes
480.notes: Read all six table rows: joint variables/configuration/no intermediate IK/simple/EE not explicit/generally nonlinear versus pose/task/IK/more complex/explicit path/Jacobian mapping. f inverse is schematic branch-solving notation, not proof of unique inverse.

481.title: Joint Space Schemes
481.notes: Joint trajectory vector theta1..thetan; independently interpolated cubic/quintic; specified position/velocity endpoints. Diagram has same endpoints t0/theta0 and tf/thetaf, blue overshoots then undershoots, red initially dips, green monotonic; positions alone do not select one shape.

482.title: Joint Space Scheme (Continued)
482.notes: Forward kinematics x(t)=f(theta(t)); printed “nonlinear and unpredictable” must mean not directly prescribed, since known f/theta determine motion. Smooth torque claim presumes continuous dynamics and no unmodeled jumps, not arbitrary actuator feasibility.

483.title: Trajectory Problem Formulation
483.notes: Initial/final joint angles and time, optional endpoint velocities, interval[0,tf], minimum C1/preferred C2, rest-to-rest sets both endpoint velocities zero.

484.title: General Boundary Conditions and Polynomial Count
484.notes: General endpoint velocities omega0/omegaf need not zero. Polynomial degree n has n+1 coefficients; 2/4/6 counts map linear/cubic/quintic. Printed count-equality statement requires independent compatible constraints for uniqueness, not merely equal raw number.

485.title: Why Cubic?
485.notes: Four endpoint position/velocity conditions require four independent coefficients generically; degrees1,2,3 give2,3,4. General cubic printed. Lower degree can satisfy special compatible data; uniqueness presumes tf>0.

486.title: Cubic Polynomial Via Point
486.notes: Via points theta_i at t_i, one cubic between consecutive points; via velocities not fixed by positions alone and must assigned/computed. Segment-local versus global time must be explicitly distinguished in using zero-time formulas.

487.title: Cubic Boundary Equations
487.notes: Read cubic and its first/second derivatives. Four numbered equations: a0=theta0,a1=v0, final position and final velocity. Final position coefficients tf,tf²,tf³; derivative2a2tf+3a3tf².

488.title: Cubic Coefficient Elimination
488.notes: Defines residual Delta theta=thetaf−theta0−v0tf and Delta v=vf−v0; divided equations and subtract twice first yields a3=Delta v/tf²−2Delta theta/tf³. These are correct, but Delta theta is not plain displacement for nonzero v0.

489.title: Derivation (Continued)
489.notes: Back substitution gives correct a2=[3(thetaf−theta0)−(2v0+vf)tf]/tf² and a3=[−2(thetaf−theta0)+(v0+vf)tf]/tf³. Position-versus-time plot is monotonic S-shaped illustration, not guaranteed by arbitrary endpoint velocities.

490.title: Rest-to-Rest Cubic and Velocity Profile
490.notes: Zero endpoint velocities give a0=theta0,a1=0,a2=3Delta/tf²,a3=−2Delta/tf³; theta=theta0+3Delta(t/tf)²−2Delta(t/tf)³. Velocity6Delta t/tf²(1−t/tf), parabolic positive-displacement sketch; Delta now equals plain displacement because v0=0.

491.title: Cubic Peak Velocity and Acceleration
491.notes: Peak at tf/2 with3Delta/(2tf); acceleration6Delta/tf²(1−2t/tf), endpoints±6Delta/tf², midpoint0. Plot linear descending, deg/s². Maximum signed velocity assumes Delta>0; for negative move midpoint is minimum signed velocity but maximum speed.

492.title: Methods of Joint Velocity Profile Generation
492.notes: Three methods explicitly listed: user-specified Cartesian-to-joint velocities, heuristic assignment, acceleration-continuous spline. Four BCs for each cubic; multisegment joins need enforced continuity. Segment duration/local time must not be mistaken for global endpoint time.

493.title: Higher-Order Polynomial Trajectories (Quintic)
493.notes: Six coefficients a0..a5, endpoints position/velocity/acceleration, correct first and second derivatives (4,5 and12,20 coefficients); six linear equations unique for distinct endpoints tf>0, not from equation count alone.

494.title: Derivation of Linear Trajectory
494.notes: First-order interpolation a0=theta0,a1=(thetaf−theta0)/tf; constant slope and zero acceleration within segment. Diagram axes theta vs t with endpoint t0 but derivation fixes t0=0. Outside rest conditions introduced on next page.

495.title: Critical Drawbacks
495.notes: Rest-to-rest nonzero linear segment jumps from0 toDelta/tf and back; continuous position but notC1 at joins, impulsive acceleration/torque idealization. “Only C0” needs the stated rest extension; isolated linear polynomial is smooth. Blending named remedy.

496.title: Numerical Example
496.notes: Exact example 10 degrees to70 degrees in5 seconds with zero endpoint velocities, cubic ansatz. No extra acceleration boundary constraints given.

497.notes: Example a0=10,a1=0; final equations25a2+125a3=60 and10a2+75a3=0; a2=−7.5a3, with coefficients dimensional when degrees and seconds used.

498.title: Numerical Example Continued
498.notes: Correct elimination−62.5a3=60 gives a3−.96 and a2 7.2; theta10+7.2t²−.96t³, velocity14.4t−2.88t², acceleration14.4−5.76t.

499.notes: Actual image code imports numpy/pyplot; inputs10,70,0,0,tf5; a0/a1 initial values; 2x2A=[[tf**2,tf**3],[2*tf,3*tf**2]], B=[theta_f−a0−a1*tf,theta_dot_f−a1]; [a2,a3]=np.linalg.solve(A,B); t=np.linspace(0,tf,100); vectorized position and analytical derivatives. Code is syntactically correct as printed. Even sample count omits midpoint2.5.

502.notes: Repeats planning comparison/linear drawbacks; cubic continuous-acceleration wording needs within-segment versus joins qualification. Quintic supports prescribed endpoint acceleration and C2 joins only when adjacent position/velocity/acceleration values match.
